segments.speaker: Raj
segments.text: Good afternoon, everyone. This is the steering committee for the office move, and we have six items today. Let's start with the timeline.

segments.speaker: Olivia
segments.text: The landlord has confirmed we can get the keys on the first of February. The fit-out will take about eight weeks after that.

segments.speaker: Raj
segments.text: So we'd move in at the start of April?

segments.speaker: James
segments.text: Early April, yes, assuming the council approves the plans for the kitchen and the bathrooms.

segments.speaker: Frank
segments.text: When do we expect the council decision?

segments.speaker: Niamh
segments.text: They said four to six weeks. We submitted the plans last Monday.

segments.speaker: Emily
segments.text: Okay. Olivia, what does that mean for the lease on the current office?

segments.speaker: Raj
segments.text: Our current lease ends on the thirty first of March. We can extend month to month, but the rent goes up by twenty percent.

segments.speaker: James
segments.text: Twenty percent is steep. Is that negotiable?

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: I've asked. They'll come back to me next week. Worst case, one extra month costs us about nine thousand dollars.

segments.speaker: Oliver
segments.text: Let's plan for one extra month as a contingency, and hope we don't need it.

segments.speaker: Emily
segments.text: Can I raise the network setup? That's the thing most likely to delay us.

segments.speaker: Kate
segments.text: Go ahead, Raj.

segments.speaker: Niamh
segments.text: The building has fibre, but the provider needs ten weeks' notice to connect us. If we order it after the keys, we'll miss April.

segments.speaker: Olivia
segments.text: Can we order it before we have the keys?

segments.speaker: James
segments.text: Yes, if the landlord signs the access form. I sent it to them on Tuesday, but I haven't heard back.

segments.speaker: Niamh
segments.text: I'll chase the landlord tomorrow. I'm meeting their property manager anyway.

segments.speaker: Olivia
segments.text: Thanks, Frank. If we get the form signed this week, we're fine.

segments.speaker: Niamh
segments.text: Good. Next item, furniture. Thandi, you were collecting quotes.

segments.speaker: Emily
segments.text: I have three quotes. The cheapest is forty two thousand, and the one I'd recommend is fifty one thousand, because it includes installation.

segments.speaker: Frank
segments.text: What's the difference in quality?

segments.speaker: Oliver
segments.text: The desks are the same. The recommended one has better chairs and a five year warranty, instead of two years.

segments.speaker: Niamh
segments.text: Then I think the extra cost is worth it, especially with the installation included.

segments.speaker: Emily
segments.text: I agree. Installation alone would cost us five or six thousand otherwise.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Any objections to going with the fifty one thousand dollar quote?

segments.speaker: James
segments.text: No objections.

segments.speaker: Olivia
segments.text: None from me.

segments.speaker: Kate
segments.text: Then that's decided. Thandi, please accept that quote and ask for delivery in the last week of March.

segments.speaker: James
segments.text: Will do. I'll send the purchase order to finance by Wednesday.

segments.speaker: Raj
segments.text: Next, the seating plan. James, you were going to survey the teams.

segments.speaker: Olivia
segments.text: Yes. About seventy percent of people want to keep fixed desks, and thirty percent are happy to hot desk.

segments.speaker: Emily
segments.text: The sales team wants to sit near the meeting rooms, and the engineers want the quiet corner away from the kitchen.

segments.speaker: Raj
segments.text: Very much so.

segments.speaker: Kate
segments.text: That seems reasonable. Can you draft a seating plan for the next meeting?

segments.speaker: Emily
segments.text: I can have a first draft by the twentieth of January.

segments.speaker: James
segments.text: Great. Olivia, the budget. Where do we stand overall?

segments.speaker: Olivia
segments.text: The approved budget is three hundred and twenty thousand. With the furniture decision, we've committed two hundred and ninety.

segments.speaker: Emily
segments.text: That leaves thirty thousand for contingencies, which is a bit thin given the lease risk.

segments.speaker: Raj
segments.text: The fit-out quote also has a ten percent allowance for surprises, so we have some cushion there.

segments.speaker: Frank
segments.text: Okay. Let's keep an eye on it, and report back if the contingency drops below twenty thousand.

segments.speaker: Niamh
segments.text: One open question from my side. Are we keeping the old furniture, or selling it?

segments.speaker: Raj
segments.text: Good question. I don't think we've decided.

segments.speaker: Kate
segments.text: Some of it could go to the Sydney office. They asked for desks last year.

segments.speaker: Emily
segments.text: Let's find out what Sydney actually needs before we decide. Can someone ask them?

segments.speaker: Raj
segments.text: I'll ask the Sydney office manager this week.

segments.speaker: Olivia
segments.text: Thank you. Last item, communication to staff. I'd like to send an update before Christmas.

segments.speaker: Niamh
segments.text: I can write the first draft, and include the seating survey results.

segments.speaker: Emily
segments.text: Perfect. Let me summarise the actions. Frank chases the landlord about the fibre access form tomorrow.

segments.speaker: Frank
segments.text: Thandi accepts the furniture quote, sends the purchase order by Wednesday, and asks Sydney about the old furniture.

segments.speaker: Emily
segments.text: James drafts the seating plan by the twentieth of January and writes the staff update. Olivia follows up on the lease extension next week.

segments.speaker: Frank
segments.text: And Raj orders the fibre as soon as the form is signed.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Yes, the same day.

segments.speaker: Olivia
segments.text: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll meet again in two weeks.

segments.speaker: James
segments.text: Morning everyone. Let's get started, we've got a lot to cover before the launch. Raj, do you want to begin with the release status?

segments.speaker: Niamh
segments.text: Sure. The release candidate went out to the beta group on Monday. We've had about three hundred people install it so far.

segments.speaker: Emily
segments.text: Crash rates are low, under half a percent, but there's one issue with the sync on older tablets that we need to fix.

segments.speaker: Olivia
segments.text: How serious is the tablet issue?

segments.speaker: Emily
segments.text: It only happens when the battery saver is on. The sync stops in the background and doesn't resume until you open the app.

segments.speaker: Niamh
segments.text: That sounds like the background limits changed in the last system update.

segments.speaker: Frank
segments.text: Yes, exactly, that's our theory too. I think we can work around it, but it'll take a few days.

segments.speaker: Raj
segments.text: Okay. Is that a blocker for the launch on the twentieth?

segments.speaker: James
segments.text: I don't think so. It affects maybe two percent of users, and they don't lose any data. It just syncs later.

segments.speaker: Olivia
segments.text: From the support side, I'd rather we ship with a known issue than delay. We can put a note in the help centre.

segments.speaker: Emily
segments.text: Agreed. Let's keep the launch date of October the twentieth, and treat the tablet sync as a fast follow.

segments.speaker: Thandi
segments.text: Okay, I'll plan the fix for the first patch release.

segments.speaker: James
segments.text: James, where are we on the marketing assets?

segments.speaker: Emily
segments.text: The landing page is done and the screenshots are being updated this week. The launch video is the one I'm worried about.

segments.speaker: Olivia
segments.text: Why is that?

segments.speaker: Raj
segments.text: The agency sent the first cut yesterday and it uses the old onboarding screens. They need the new ones from design.

segments.speaker: Olivia
segments.text: Mm-hm.

segments.speaker: Kate
segments.text: If they get the new screens by Thursday, they can still deliver the final version by the fifteenth.

segments.speaker: Niamh
segments.text: Who owns getting them the screens?

segments.speaker: James
segments.text: That's me. I'll get the exported screens from the design team and send them over by Thursday.

segments.speaker: Raj
segments.text: Great. Niamh, how is support preparing for the launch?

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: We've written twelve new help articles, and the team has done two training sessions on the new features.

segments.speaker: Raj
segments.text: My main concern is staffing. Last launch, our ticket volume tripled in the first week.

segments.speaker: Niamh
segments.text: Do we have extra people lined up?

segments.speaker: Emily
segments.text: Two people from the sales team volunteered to help with the chat queue. I'd like one more, ideally someone technical.

segments.speaker: Raj
segments.text: I could lend you one of the engineers for the first three days. Maybe Tom, he knows the sync code really well.

segments.speaker: Olivia
segments.text: That would be brilliant, thank you.

segments.speaker: Raj
segments.text: Good. Raj, can you confirm with Tom this week?

segments.speaker: Emily
segments.text: Yes, I'll ask him today.

segments.speaker: Olivia
segments.text: Next, budget. We're about fifteen thousand dollars over on the launch budget, mostly because of the video.

segments.speaker: Oliver
segments.text: Some of that is the reshoot. The original agency quote didn't include the second day of filming.

segments.speaker: Olivia
segments.text: Can we cover it from the events budget? The conference in December was cancelled.

segments.speaker: Emily
segments.text: I think so, but finance needs to approve moving the money.

segments.speaker: Raj
segments.text: Then I'll raise it with finance on Friday. If they say no, we'll cut the paid social campaign instead.

segments.speaker: Emily
segments.text: Can I ask one question about the launch day itself? Are we doing the announcement in the morning or the afternoon?

segments.speaker: Olivia
segments.text: That's not decided yet. The press team wants the morning, but our users are mostly in the US, so the afternoon might be better.

segments.speaker: Oliver
segments.text: From an engineering view, the morning is better. If something goes wrong, we have the whole day to fix it.

segments.speaker: Raj
segments.text: That's a fair point. Let's leave it open for now, and I'll decide with the press team by Monday.

segments.speaker: Olivia
segments.text: Okay, let me summarise. Launch stays on the twentieth. Raj fixes the tablet sync in the first patch and confirms Tom for support.

segments.speaker: Raj
segments.text: James sends the new screens to the agency by Thursday. I'll talk to finance on Friday and decide the announcement time by Monday.

segments.speaker: Olivia
segments.text: And I'll publish the help articles the day before launch.

segments.speaker: Thandi
segments.text: Perfect. Thanks everyone, same time next week.

segments.speaker: Kate
segments.text: Thanks for making time, James. I wanted to go through the cloud hosting renewal before the end of the month.

segments.speaker: Thandi
segments.text: Sure. I had a look at the quote they sent on Friday. It's about eighteen percent higher than last year.

segments.speaker: Olivia
segments.text: That's more than I expected. Did they explain where the increase comes from?

segments.speaker: Niamh
segments.text: Mostly storage. Our backups have doubled since March, and they've moved us onto a new pricing tier.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Right.

segments.speaker: Emily
segments.text: The compute part is actually a little cheaper, because we committed to reserved instances last spring.

segments.speaker: James
segments.text: Okay. So if we cleaned up the old backups, how much of that would we save?

segments.speaker: Niamh
segments.text: Probably a third of the increase. We keep ninety days of snapshots, and nobody has restored anything older than two weeks.

segments.speaker: Thandi
segments.text: Then let's cut the retention to thirty days. Can you check with the security team that thirty days still meets the audit requirements?

segments.speaker: Niamh
segments.text: Yes, I'll ask Priya today. She did the last audit, so she'll know.

segments.speaker: Frank
segments.text: Great. And what about the alternative provider? Did you get a number from them?

segments.speaker: Raj
segments.text: I did. They're about ten percent cheaper on paper, but the migration would take at least six weeks of engineering time.

segments.speaker: Frank
segments.text: Six weeks is a lot. We don't have that before the product launch in November.

segments.speaker: Oliver
segments.text: Exactly. My suggestion is to renew for one year, not three, and revisit the move in the spring.

segments.speaker: Olivia
segments.text: I agree. Let's renew for one year. I'll sign the contract once the retention change is confirmed.

segments.speaker: Kate
segments.text: Sounds good.

segments.speaker: Thandi
segments.text: The other thing I wanted to talk about is hiring. How are the interviews for the platform engineer going?

segments.speaker: Kate
segments.text: We've had four candidates so far. Two were strong, and one of them, Marco, has done exactly this kind of migration before.

segments.speaker: Emily
segments.text: That would be useful if we do move providers next year.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: That's what I thought. I'd like to bring him in for the final round next week, if you can join.

segments.speaker: Frank
segments.text: I can do Tuesday or Thursday afternoon. Wednesday is full of budget meetings.

segments.speaker: Oliver
segments.text: Let's say Thursday at two. I'll send the invite and the take-home task results.

segments.speaker: James
segments.text: Perfect. Is there anything blocking you that I can help with?

segments.speaker: Niamh
segments.text: Just one thing. The finance team still hasn't approved the monitoring tool we asked for in August.

segments.speaker: Emily
segments.text: I'll chase that with Daniel in finance. I think it's stuck because the request went to the wrong cost centre.

segments.speaker: Niamh
segments.text: That would explain it. Thanks.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Okay, so to recap. You'll confirm the thirty day retention with Priya, and send me the updated quote by Friday.

segments.speaker: Emily
segments.text: Yes. And I'll set up the final interview with Marco for Thursday at two.

segments.speaker: James
segments.text: And I'll sort out the monitoring tool approval. Thanks, James, that was really helpful.

segments.speaker: Emily
segments.text: Thanks, Sarah. Talk soon.
